reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law (expressly listed in the playbook fallback) with exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and federal courts in New York, New York (the preferred forum), so the clause meets the fallback on its material terms.

Consistent with the retention rule for fallback-level clauses, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and the deterministic accepted-jurisdiction check passes.

The Section 8 AAA arbitration provision is correctly analyzed as domestic (no foreign seat), so it does not reach the walk-away position on mandatory arbitration seated abroad; the drafting tension with the exclusive-court forum is appropriately noted in the rationale rather than escalated to a deviation.

Rationale is accurate and internally consistent: it identifies Delaware as fallback rather than preferred New York law and flags the sub-element as a record note only, matching the playbook's classification semantics.
